questions.question: A boy covers a certain distance between his house and school on a cycle. Riding on an average speed of 15 km/h, he is late by 10 min. However, with an average speed of 20 km/h, he reaches the school 5 min earlier. Find the distance between his house and school.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For problems involving **Late** and **Early** reaching times, the distance is calculated as:

**Distance** = [(S₁ × S₂) / (S₂ − S₁)] × [Total Time Difference / 60]

Total time difference = 10 min (late) + 5 min (early) = 15 min.

Distance = [(15 × 20) / (20 − 15)] × (15 / 60) = (300 / 5) × (1 / 4) = 60 / 4 = 15 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Speed 1 (S₁)** = 15 km/h (Late by 10 min)

**Speed 2 (S₂)** = 20 km/h (Early by 5 min)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0b99236afd48e39807918b797defdb75b261956c48e8694dec3ef2b3719afda7.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the **Distance** be 'D' km.

Time taken at 15 km/h = D / 15

Time taken at 20 km/h = D / 20

The difference between being 10 min late and 5 min early is 15 minutes.

⇒ (D / 15) − (D / 20) = 15 / 60

⇒ (D / 15) − (D / 20) = 1 / 4

Taking LCM of 15 and 20, which is 60:

⇒ (4D − 3D) / 60 = 1 / 4

⇒ D / 60 = 1 / 4

⇒ D = 60 / 4

⇒ D = 15 km

**∴ The correct answer is 15 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Time Difference Rule

When one case is **late** and another is **early**, add the times. If both are late or both are early, subtract the times to find the net difference.

Speed-Time Relation

For a constant distance, speed is **inversely proportional** to time (S₁ / S₂ = T₂ / T₁).

Conversion Units

To convert **km/h** to **m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert minutes to hours, divide by 60.</p

questions.question: The sum of the radius of the base and the height of a cylinder is 42 m. If the total surface area of the cylinder is 6336 m², find the curved surface area of the cylinder correct to two places of decimals (use π = (22)/(7)).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The radius + height = 42 m.

The total surface area = 6336 m2,

**Concept used:**

The total surface area of the cylinder = curved surface area of the cylinder + area of the base

**Formula used:**

The curved surface area = 2πrh (r= radius and h = height)

**Calculation:** 

As per the question,

 r + h = 42

Again,

2πr (r + h) = 6336 

⇒ 2πr × 42 = 6336

⇒ r = 6336 / 264

⇒ r = 24

Then h = 42 - 24

⇒ 18m

The curved surface area will be , 2πrh

⇒ 2 × 22/7 × 18 × 24 = 2715.43 m2

**∴ The correct option is** 3

questions.question: If cos A = (63)/(65), then find the value of tan A + cot A (up to two places of decimal).
questions.solution:
**Concept used:**

**Tan A = Sin A / Cos A**

**Calculation:**

 cos A = (63)/(65), Then sin A = (16)/(65)

Then , 

tan A + cot A = (sin A / cos A) + (cos A / sin A)

⇒ 16/65 × 65/63 + 63/65 × 65/16

⇒ 16/ 63 + 63 / 16 = 4.19

**∴ The correct option is** **1**

questions.question: The ratio of cost price (CP) and marked price (MP) of an article is 4 ∶ 7. A discount of 20% is given on MP and the shopkeeper made a profit of ₹80. Find the CP of the article.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__
Let CP and MP of the article be 400 and 700 units respectively.

Discount = 20% of 700 = 140 units, so SP = 700 − 140 = 560 units.

Profit = SP − CP = 560 − 400 = 160 units.

Given, 160 units = ₹80 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹0.5.

Cost price (CP) = 400 units × 0.5 = ₹200.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of Cost Price (CP) to Marked Price (MP) = 4 : 7

Discount = 20%

Profit = ₹80

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount

Profit = SP − CP

CP = 4xSP = 5.6xMP = 7x
• Profit1.6x
• Discount20%Profit = 1.6x = ₹80, so x = 50
**Calculation:**

⇒ Let CP = 4x and MP = 7x

⇒ Discount is given on the Marked Price

⇒ Discount = 20% of 7x = (20 ÷ 100) × 7x = 1.4x

⇒ SP = MP − Discount = 7x − 1.4x = 5.6x

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 5.6x − 4x = 1.6x

⇒ We are given that Profit = ₹80

⇒ 1.6x = 80

⇒ x = 80 ÷ 1.6 = 50

⇒ Cost Price (CP) = 4x = 4 × 50 = 200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Profit & Loss Base

Profit or Loss is always evaluated on the Cost Price (CP) unless stated otherwise. Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Successive Discount

When two successive discounts d₁% and d₂% are given, the Equivalent Single Discount = (d₁ + d₂ − d₁×d₂ ÷ 100)%.

questions.question: A man deposited ₹10,000 at simple interest in a fund. The interest rate on the fund increases by 4% every year. If the interest rate at the time of the amount deposit was 8%, what is the interest earned (in ₹) by him after 5 years?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Effective **Interest Rate** = 8% + 12% + 16% + 20% + 24% = 80%

Total **Interest Earned** = 80% of ₹10,000

⇒ Total Interest = (80 ÷ 100) × 10,000 = ₹8,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹8,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹10,000

**Initial Rate (R₁)** = 8%

**Annual Increment** = 4%

**Time (T)** = 5 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/429a6dd79549cbfb1467ed7cacd13310828164353e8484368c12b747edf845ae.png] 

**Step-by-step Calculation:**

⇒ Interest for 1st Year = (10,000 × 8 × 1) ÷ 100 = ₹800

⇒ Interest for 2nd Year = (10,000 × 12 × 1) ÷ 100 = ₹1,200

⇒ Interest for 3rd Year = (10,000 × 16 × 1) ÷ 100 = ₹1,600

⇒ Interest for 4th Year = (10,000 × 20 × 1) ÷ 100 = ₹2,000

⇒ Interest for 5th Year = (10,000 × 24 × 1) ÷ 100 = ₹2,400

⇒ **Total Interest Earned** = 800 + 1,200 + 1,600 + 2,000 + 2,400

⇒ Total Interest Earned = ₹8,000

Therefore, the total interest earned after 5 years is ₹8,000, which corresponds to **Option 4**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹8,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest vs. Compound Interest

In **Simple Interest**, the interest is calculated only on the initial principal. In **Compound Interest**, interest is calculated on the principal plus the accumulated interest of previous periods.

Arithmetic Progression of Rates

When rates increase by a constant amount, the total rate is the sum of an AP: Sₙ = n/2 × [2a + (n−1)d]. Here, n=5, a=8, d=4, so Sₙ = 5/2 × [16 + 16] = 80%.

Effective Annual Rate

The effective average interest rate over the period is Total Rate ÷ Total Years. Here, 80% ÷ 5 = 16% per annum.

questions.question: Find the average of the prime numbers lying between 51 and 77.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify **prime numbers** between 51 and 77: 53, 59, 61, 67, 71, 73.

**Sum** of these 6 numbers = 53 + 59 + 61 + 67 + 71 + 73 = 384.

**Average** = Total Sum ÷ Number of terms = 384 ÷ 6 = 64.

**∴ The correct answer is 64.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Range for prime numbers is 51 to 77.

**Formula:** Average = (Sum of observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1a9f3889dcdae1bcb7179d7fa4337ece4120c86366325c4b97b1dd6d423f51a1.png] 

⇒ Prime numbers are 53, 59, 61, 67, 71, and 73.

⇒ Sum = 53 + 59 + 61 + 67 + 71 + 73 = 384.

⇒ Number of terms = 6.

⇒ Average = 384 ÷ 6

⇒ Average = 64.

**∴ The correct answer is 64.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Prime Numbers

A **prime number** is a natural number greater than 1 that has no positive divisors other than 1 and itself. The smallest prime number is 2.

Arithmetic Mean

The **Average** (Arithmetic Mean) is the ratio of the **sum** of all observations to the **total number** of observations.

Prime Checklist

To check if a number **n** is prime, test for divisibility by all prime numbers less than or equal to √n.</p
